title: Stage 5 — Deployment
goal: Ship your app beyond localhost: production builds, environment variables, and live URLs.
summary: Deploy the API and frontend, configure secrets safely, and prove the full stack works in production.

pages.title: Why deploy before you feel ready

checkpoint.prompt: Why put the database URL in an environment variable instead of hardcoding it in source?

choices.text: So dev, staging, and production can use different values without code changes
Because environment variables make the app run faster

checkpoint.explanation: Config differs per environment. Code stays the same; the host injects the right values at runtime.

checkpoint.prompt: You need an API key for production. What should you do?

choices.text: Set it in the host's environment / secrets UI — never commit it
Commit it to main so deploys are automatic
Paste it in the README for your future self

checkpoint.explanation: Secrets in git leak forever in history. Hosts like Railway, Render, and Vercel have secrets panels for a reason.

checkpoint.prompt: In production, Next.js typically runs `next build` then `next start`. Why not `next dev`?

choices.text: `next dev` is unoptimized and unsafe for real users; the build produces optimized output

checkpoint.explanation: Dev servers trade speed for safety and performance. Production builds bundle, minify, and catch issues early.

checkpoint.prompt: Your frontend is at https://myapp.vercel.app and API at https://api.railway.app. The browser blocks requests. Likely cause?

choices.text: API CORS only allows localhost — production origin must be added
You must merge frontend and API into one repo file

checkpoint.explanation: Browsers enforce CORS. Your API must explicitly allow the production frontend origin.

checkpoint.prompt: After deploying, what is the simplest check that the API is alive? (one GET path)
checkpoint.explanation: A health endpoint (or hitting your root GET) confirms the process is up before you debug the full UI flow.

checklist.label: API deployed with a public HTTPS URL
Frontend deployed with a public HTTPS URL
Production env vars set on the host (no secrets in git)
API allows the production frontend origin
Created a record through the live site end to end

questions.prompt: What belongs in environment variables instead of source code?

choices.text: Database URLs, API keys, and other config that changes per environment

questions.explanation: Environment-specific and secret config goes in env vars. Logic stays in code.

questions.prompt: Should `.env` files with real secrets be committed to Git?

choices.text: No — use .env.example with placeholders; real values only on the host

questions.explanation: Even private repos leak. Use .env.example for documentation; inject real secrets at deploy time.

questions.prompt: Why run a production build before deploy?

choices.text: To catch build errors early and serve optimized assets

questions.explanation: CI/build steps surface TypeScript and bundling failures before users hit them.

questions.prompt: Why do production apps use HTTPS?

choices.text: Encrypts traffic and is required for many browser features (cookies, secure APIs)

questions.explanation: HTTPS protects data in transit. Modern hosts provide certificates automatically.

questions.prompt: You updated the API URL the frontend calls. What must you redeploy?

choices.text: The frontend (it bakes in or reads the API URL at build/runtime)

questions.explanation: If the frontend's API base URL changed, rebuild/redeploy the frontend with the new config.
